caveats: Run with --jobs 3 instead of the default 6; results do not depend on the job count.
The golden CPU is flagged in race_ext_0 (the race probe sw zero,4(s11)), not in race_timer_0 or race_both_0; that flag is the expected bounded-latency race, not a tagged golden deviation.
test/trapsweep/README.md:56 shows --seeds 301-330 for the bp fuzz example while its results line (176) uses 301-360; the 301-360 range was run.

sweep.py excuses the race family on the DUT only (dut_ok = ok or fam in EXPECTED; ref_ok = ok), so race_ext_0 is one of the 26 golden programs counted as not ISS-consistent (results.json: dut_ok true, ref_ok false); docs/VERIFICATION.md:119 holds for 25 of the 26

Correction (2026-10-01): the fuzz commands were first recorded without --out; all four sets then share build/trapsweep/fuzz/ and each replaces the previous set's results.json and summary.txt. Each set now has its own --out directory, as in results/check.sh, which derives results.csv, flags.txt and fuzz.csv from those directories and compares them (make check-results CHECK_ARGS=trapsweep).
